goal: zig-waf runs OWASP CRS at least as fast as ModSecurity 3.0.16 per request, measured by the benchmark lab, with the form and JSON body paths fixed first.
scope: Profile the crs-get, crs-form-post and crs-json-post scenarios and record where each request's time and bytes go
Cut per-request allocation on the CRS path: zig-waf allocates 1.1 MiB per clean GET and 3.8 MiB per 973-byte form, against ModSecurity's 0.9 and 1.8 MiB
Fix the body path first: the form takes 8.4 ms against ModSecurity's 1.5 ms, and the JSON body 11.1 ms against 4.8 ms
Then the header and URI path: a clean GET takes 1.42 ms against ModSecurity's 0.80 ms and Coraza's 0.66 ms
Record before and after numbers from `zig build lab` in docs/benchmark-lab.md for each change
out_of_scope: Moving @pm and phrase matching onto zig-regex literals (P9.09)
Changing any rule decision: the lab's zero-mismatch rule holds throughout
notes: First lab results (zig-utils/zig-waf#6, zig-waf f6a40a2, CRS 4.28.0 at PL1, one Apple M-series run under load): zig-waf is the cheapest engine with no rules (3.0 µs and 8 allocations per request) and loads CRS fastest, so the gap is in rule evaluation, not embedding or loading
zig-waf makes fewer allocation calls than ModSecurity on a GET (6,222 against 11,557) but more bytes, so allocation size and copying matter more than count
The lab runs only on a machine with ModSecurity, Coraza and a CRS checkout; P9.38 puts it in CI
accept: `zig build lab` shows zig-waf's p50 at or below ModSecurity's on crs-get, crs-form-post and crs-json-post, on the same machine and run
Zero mismatches across every lab scenario, and the FTW and differential suites still pass
docs/benchmark-lab.md records the new results and what changed

goal: The three-engine benchmark lab runs in CI, so every change to zig-waf's request path is checked against ModSecurity and Coraza for decisions and recorded for speed.
scope: A CI job that builds ModSecurity 3.0.16 and Coraza 3.7.0 at the commits CI already pins, checks out CRS 4.28.0, and runs `zig build lab -Doptimize=ReleaseFast`
Cache the libmodsecurity build so the job does not rebuild it on every run
Fail the job on any engine error or decision mismatch
Upload results.md and results.json as an artifact
out_of_scope: Failing CI on latency regressions: shared runners are too noisy for a timing gate
notes: The lab needs Zig 0.17.0-dev.1857 or newer because zig-bench, its memory sampler, requires it
Left out of zig-utils/zig-waf#6 because GitHub Actions did not start runs for recent pushes to zig-utils repositories, so a new job could not be tried
accept: The lab job runs on pushes to main and passes with zero mismatches
A run's results.md and results.json are downloadable from the job
A deliberately wrong expected decision in a scenario fails the job
